newsitem.title: USA: CRAY says US finds Japan dumping computers.
newsitem.headline: CRAY says US finds Japan dumping computers.

text.p: Cray Research Inc on Monday said the U.S. Department of Commerce found preliminary evidence of dumping of supercomputers in the U.S. market by NEC Corp and Fujitsu Ltd of Japan.

"The findings announced today by the Commerce Department confirm what we have contended since last July -- namely that the four vector supercomputers offered to the University Corp for Atmospheric Research (UCAR) by NEC were illegally dumped," Cray Research President Robert Ewald said in a statement.
NEC won the UCAR contract, outbidding Cray, a subsidiary of Silicon Graphics, Inc. and Fujistu.
Cray said the Commerce Department found that NEC and Fujitsu had offered vector supercomputers for sale to U.S. customers at less than fair value.

The preliminary ruling means U.S. Customs will begin collecting a cash deposit or bond on supercomputers exported to the United States from the two Japanese companies pending a final ruling in the case.
